goal: Make corrupted database reads fatal instead of silently returning missing/false, so operators get a clear crash instead of hidden wrong answers
Closes a gap left by an earlier fix that only covered unreadable coins, extending fatal handling to indexes and chainstate
reviewability: Ready: CI passes, branch is clean and mergeable, and nine months of review comments have been iterated through
An open design question about aborting on optional-index corruption remains but the author has deferred it, not paused the PR
agreement: Strong support for removing the read-error indirection and closing the silent-corruption gap (andrewtoth)
ACK and later reACK after rebase (optout21)
Nonblocking objection: aborting the whole node for a corrupt optional index may be too harsh (ajtowns)
Commit-hygiene and test-behavior concerns raised and resolved through rewrites (maflcko)

categories.name: indexes
why: P2 because it stops optional indexes (txindex, blockfilter, coinstats) from silently returning wrong answers on corruption
Benefits anyone relying on index-backed RPCs by turning masked corruption into a clear failure
Impact is tempered by an open debate over whether aborting the whole node is the right response for an optional index

categories.name: validation
why: P2 because a corrupted UTXO database read can currently be silently treated as a missing coin, risking confusing wrong answers
Protects chainstate correctness by making read failures abort rather than masquerade as normal misses
Scope is narrowed since it requires actual on-disk corruption, a rare condition, and abort-scope design is still debated
